text:
Matthew Kessel is a fifth-round pick of the Blues out of UMass who has worked his way into an Islanders lineup decimated by injuries. In 10 games he has three assists, playing about 13 and a half minutes a night, mostly on the third pair, with occasional penalty-kill shifts.

The on-ice numbers are excellent for a depth defenseman: the Islanders have taken 61% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly 13 points better than without him. In 10 games of sheltered minutes, that comes with a large asterisk, and we'd treat it as encouraging rather than proof.

Evolving-Hockey had too little of him last season to judge (364 minutes in St. Louis), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from eight games, shows him exiting the zone with possession half the time. NHL Edge rates his shot harder than 84% of the league, though he has yet to score. Our range says 10 to 24 points over a full season. With Ryan Pulock out for weeks, he'll keep getting looks, and so far he's making the most of easy minutes.
headline: Kessel makes the most of his minutes
